readings_ruling: Both marks hold. Statements were read against the transcription (l.451–491) and against the scan's page images (journal pp. 252–253 = PDF pp. 25–26, rendered at 90 dpi). The scan prints « tel que gE ⊂ P » and « gM ∈ P; gN ∈ P », as transcribed. Reading « ⊂ » as ⊆ is the paper's own. It is Bourbaki's non-strict inclusion. (1) l.129 « φ(P) ⊂ H̊ » is met with equality by the paper's own pocket (ℝⁿ, H₀, j, 0). (2) In 3° (l.237) « (M, N) ⊂ (M', N') » carries the conclusion ≤, so it covers the equal case. (3) l.549 restates Prop. 7 as « l'image par g du lacet … soit dans P, g[M, M] ⊂ P ». (4) Ch. 1 Déf. 15 calls « balayable » the case G₁ = G of « balayable pour un sous-groupe G₁ ⊂ G ». A strict ⊊ would even make the statement false at n = 0: V = P = E is one point. « connexe » read as PreconnectedSpace V is a genuine weakening, since the empty V is allowed and is excluded anyway by the nonempty pocket. « compact » read as IsCompact is a weakening: quasi-compact, with Bourbaki's Hausdorff condition dropped. « variété » without T2 or second countability is a weakening. « un groupe G d'automorphismes projectifs » is a Subgroup of GXAut (GSR n) (S n) V (strict, Déf. 15, marked). The pocket is IsPocheProj (strict, Déf. 1′, marked). Sweepability is IsBalayableFor (strict: a compact K with ⋃_{g∈G} gK = V, word for word Déf. 15). Independence from the open questions, checked on the proof term. OQ-45: n = 0 is handled by subsingleton_dim_zero together with hP.isConnected.nonempty and g = 1. It touches neither n(E, k) nor Prop. 4, and ligne_brisee is called only under NeZero n. OQ-61: the proof takes only .2.1 of IsPocheProj.ligne_brisee_poche, that is B ∈ P. A mutant that took .1 (L ⊆ P) instead fails with type `(fun x => g • x) N ∈ P`. Under OQ-61 (a), IsPocheProj would gain a field. That strengthens the hypothesis, so the theorems stay true. The marks therefore depend on neither OQ. Non-vacuity: the marked rows carry no witness, and none is needed for the mark. The anchors are universally quantified implications whose hypotheses are the strict, separately audited predicates, so the only risk is that their conjunction is unsatisfiable. It is satisfiable in every dimension. An audit probe (/tmp, deleted) compiled with standard axioms and proved the following. In ℝⁿ with the canonical projective structure projOfAff, exists_isPocheProj_model n gives the pocket (ℝⁿ, H₀, j, 0). IsBalayableFor holds for G = ⊤ with K = {0}, because each translation x ↦ y + x is a projective morphism (Sphere.hemiChart_apply_eq_smul with GAR.translation y) and so an automorphism (GXAut.ofBijective). The probe then applied compactDansPochePrinted n to that data and the closed unit ball. The model S(n) suggested in the dispatch is NOT one: for n ≥ 1 no compact V carries a pocket. A compact V is sweepable for ⊥, so Prop. 7 forces P = V. Then φ(V) would be a compact open subset of the connected S(n) inside H̊ ⊊ S(n), which is impossible. So any witness for n ≥ 1 is non-compact. The probe used the z ≡ 0 pocket. Should OQ-61 (a) make it illegitimate, a non-constant cote still works, mathematically (not formalised): ]0, ∞[ with its homotheties, K = [1, 2], P = ]0, 1[, z = x.

labels.label: bzprop:c2s2p7_compact_dans_poche
labels.notes: Correctly MARKED. Elaborated type (#check @Benzecri.compact_dans_poche): ∀ {n} {V : Type u} [TopologicalSpace V] [ChartedSpace (S n) V] [HasGroupoid V (projGroupoid n)] {P l} [Fact (l ≠ 0)] {φ z} [PreconnectedSpace V] {G : Subgroup (GXAut (GSR n) (S n) V)}, IsBalayableFor (GSR n) (S n) V G → IsPocheProj P l φ z → ∀ {E}, IsCompact E → ∃ g ∈ G, g • E ⊆ P. Hypothesis by hypothesis against l.451–457, every hypothesis is the paper's or weaker. « variété localement projective »: the strict encoding, with T2 and second countability dropped. « connexe »: preconnected. « balayable pour un groupe G d'automorphismes projectifs (déf. 15) »: Subgroup plus IsBalayableFor. « poche »: IsPocheProj. « E un compact »: IsCompact. There is no NeZero n, so every dimension is covered. The conclusion « il existe g ∈ G tel que gE ⊂ P » is carried exactly, with ⊂ read as ⊆ (see readings_ruling). The printed form CompactDansPochePrinted n (#print) quantifies over V : Type with T2Space, ConnectedSpace and SecondCountableTopology, every G, every pocket (P, l, φ, z) and every compact E. That is the printed sentence word for word. compactDansPochePrinted n is the anchor instantiated, for every n, so it is a corollary of the anchor and not a separate claim. The lemma of the first paragraph: IsBalayableFor.exists_domaineGenerateur and exists_domaineGenerateur_proj give F ⊇ E with F compact and preconnected and ⋃_{g∈G} g•F = univ. That is « inclus dans un domaine générateur connexe », and the _isConnected form gives IsConnected F for a ConnectedSpace V. exists_isCompact_isPreconnected_superset_of_locallyConnected takes the printed hypotheses of l.465 (locally compact, locally connected, connected, plus T2). IsLigneBrisee.smul states 2° (l.234–235) lifted to broken lines, with the same k and p. The four REPORT findings are proof-level, and the statement is unaffected. (1) l.466–468 needs broken lines between arbitrary points of a connected V. That is true for n ≥ 1, by a clopen argument. The paper proves it nowhere before Prop. 7: a grep of ch1 and ch2 for « ligne brisée » finds only l.389–406 (Prop. 4, compact connected E) and l.433 (Prop. 5, asserted). Correct as a gap, not an error. (2) l.477–479: Prop. 6 has to be applied to gL, because L starts at N⁰, which need not lie in P. Two facts are left implicit: 2° (l.235), and K^p ≤ K^{n(E,k)} for K > 1. Correct. (3) Only B ∈ P is used. Correct, and verified on the proof term. (4) Dimension 0: correct under the strict library's Déf. 1 convention, but stated too categorically (finding 2). Line citations checked: l.129, 237, 432–434, 464, 466–468, 471, 475, 477–479, 549.

labels.label: bzcor:c2s2p7c_deux_points_dans_poche
labels.notes: Correctly MARKED. Elaborated type: same binders as compact_dans_poche, then ∀ (M N : V), ∃ g ∈ G, g • M ∈ P ∧ g • N ∈ P. That is « soient M et N deux points de V. Il existe un automorphisme projectif g ∈ G de V tel que gM ∈ P; gN ∈ P » (l.482–487), the « ; » read as a conjunction. M = N is allowed, which the paper does not exclude (« deux points » in the sense of two names). The proof is the paper's: {M, N} is compact (l.489–491). DeuxPointsDansPochePrinted n has the same quantifier prefix as CompactDansPochePrinted, followed by ∀ M N, …, and is proved for every n. Non-vacuity: the hypotheses are those of Prop. 7, shown jointly satisfiable above.

findings.where: REPORT.json notes ('Not given: an example that meets every hypothesis at once … That needs the affine-to-projective automorphism transfer that T-bz-c2-cas-affin lacks')
findings.what: The claim is inaccurate. The ℝⁿ model needs no transfer lemma. Under projOfAff the preferred chart of every point is hemiChart, and Sphere.hemiChart_apply_eq_smul (GAR.translation y) w gives hemiChart (y + w) = affToGS (GAR.translation y) • hemiChart w. So x ↦ y + x is an IsGXMorphism, and GXAut.ofBijective makes it an automorphism. Hence IsBalayableFor (GSR n) (S n) (Fin n → ℝ) ⊤ holds with K = {0}. Combined with exists_isPocheProj_model n, every hypothesis of CompactDansPochePrinted n is met in every dimension. The audit probe proved this (about 15 lines, standard axioms) and applied compactDansPochePrinted to it. The general transfer that T-bz-c2-cas-affin lacks, for an arbitrary locally affine V, is a different matter. The marks are not affected, since the hypotheses are satisfiable. But the sentence would mislead the planner about what non-vacuity costs.
findings.fix: In REPORT notes, replace the sentence with: 'Non-vacuity (audit): ℝⁿ with projOfAff, G = ⊤ (translations are automorphisms by Sphere.hemiChart_apply_eq_smul and GXAut.ofBijective), K = {0}, and the pocket of exists_isPocheProj_model n meet every hypothesis, in every n. No transfer lemma is needed for the model.' Optionally, at graduation, add the witness to Compact.lean as a theorem (∃ φ z, IsPocheProj univ (lastForm n) φ z ∧ IsBalayableFor (GSR n) (S n) (Fin n → ℝ) ⊤ under projOfAff), with a note that it uses the z ≡ 0 pocket and must be replaced if OQ-61 (a) is ruled.

findings.what: « In dimension 0 the printed proof does not run (n(E, k) is undefined and Prop. 4 fails, OQ-45) » is true only under the strict library's Déf. 1 convention, under which coincident points carry no measure. Under OQ-45 (b), where a point has measure 0, the one-point open set is majorised, so n({M}, k) = 1 and Prop. 4 holds at n = 0. The printed proof then runs, since it uses only B ∈ P from Prop. 6. Under OQ-45 (a), dimension 0 is excluded and the remark is moot. The parenthetical names OQ-45, but the sentence reads as an unconditional fact about the paper's proof. The claim that the statement holds in every dimension is unaffected.
findings.fix: Reword: 'Under the strict library's Déf. 1 convention (coincident points carry no measure; OQ-45 open), n(E, k) is undefined at n = 0 and Prop. 4 fails there, so the printed proof does not run. Under OQ-45 (b) it does. The statement holds at n = 0 regardless, because a connected V has at most one point.'
